abstracts.cdata!: The World Development Report 2025, titled "Standards for Development," emphasizes the critical role of standards as an invisible infrastructure for modern economies, essential for prosperity, export growth, technology diffusion, and resilient public services. The report categorizes standards into three types: measurement, compatibility, and quality, highlighting their historical evolution and increasing importance in a globalized, digitalized world. It outlines a progressive framework for countries—adapt, align, and author—to effectively leverage standards based on their economic development stage and compliance capacity. Key insights include the necessity for low- and middle-income countries to resist overregulation, focus on building "quality infrastructure" (metrology, conformity assessment, accreditation, and standardization), and actively participate in international standard-setting forums. The report stresses that while voluntary standards often drive innovation, mandatory standards are crucial for public safety and environmental protection. It also notes that compliance costs can be substantial for firms in developing countries, particularly SMEs, and that standards can act as both enablers and barriers to trade and competition. Ultimately, the report advocates for a balanced approach to standards, ensuring they serve as a springboard for development rather than a straitjacket, and calls for increased data and research on their economic and social impacts.
